title: When a Curitiba Pharmacy Began Making Its Own Creams
dek: In 1977 Miguel Krigsner opened a compounding pharmacy in Curitiba; within three years its home-made creams had an airport shop and a first franchisee.

story.event: Turning a small compounding pharmacy into a cosmetics brand sold through shops and franchises
story.summary: On 22 March 1977 the pharmacist Miguel Krigsner opened O Boticário, a compounding pharmacy on Rua Saldanha Marinho in Curitiba, reportedly with about US$3,000. He began making creams, a shampoo, a seaweed bath and the cologne Acqua Fresca under the shop's name, opened a shop at Curitiba airport in 1979, and from 1980, lacking capital, grew through franchisees, starting in Brasília, building a franchise system that he says did not yet exist in Brazil.
paragraphs: On 22 March 1977 a compounding pharmacy opened on Rua Saldanha Marinho, in the centre of Curitiba. Its owner, Miguel Krigsner, had graduated in pharmacy and biochemistry from the Federal University of Paraná two years before and started, Bloomberg Línea reports, with about US$3,000. He called it O Boticário, an old word for the pharmacist. The idea came from a course in Porto Alegre, where making up prescriptions by hand, mostly for the skin, was being rediscovered. The company's history says the shop had no counters stacked with medicines, but a carpeted room with a sofa, magazines and coffee for people waiting, and the owners served customers themselves.

Word spread, and Krigsner moved from filling prescriptions to making products under the shop's own name. According to the company, he beat the first creams in a mixer his sister had been given as a wedding present. The early range was a few creams, a shampoo, a seaweed bath and a cologne, Acqua Fresca, sold in a bottle shaped like an amphora. He later said that even in the pharmacy days he saw a chance to grow, without knowing how far it could go.

In 1979 the brand opened its own shop at Curitiba's airport. Flight attendants, a company executive later recalled, bought the products as presents and carried word of them to other cities. Krigsner wanted more shops but had no capital. In 1980 Laura Oliveira, who had found the products on a trip to Curitiba, opened an O Boticário shop in Brasília, and the franchise network began. Brazil had no franchise system then, Krigsner said: no contracts, no rules, no procedures. "A gente teve que criar do zero," he said: they had to build it from nothing. Franchisees' money let the brand grow faster than it could have alone.

Growth ran ahead of planning. He remembered the first factory as a jumble of sheds, extended each time some money came in, and said he never even had time to plan. The first shop in Portugal opened in 1985. By 2024 the group had about 4,000 shops, and Krigsner chaired its board.

quote.text: Let thy face be bright what time thou livest.  That which goeth into the storehouse must come out therefrom; and bread is to be shared.
quote.work: The Instruction of Ptahhotep (and of Ke'gemni)
quote.source_title: The Instruction of Ptah-Hotep and the Instruction of Ke'Gemni, tr. Battiscombe G. Gunn, Project Gutenberg eBook #30508
quote.connection: Ptahhotep's storehouse is meant to be emptied: what comes in must go out, and bread is shared. Krigsner's brand travelled first in flight attendants' bags and then through franchisees who, he said, often put their life savings in; it grew by letting other people carry it and own part of it.

reflection: The coffee and the sofa in that first pharmacy were a decision about how people who had to wait should be treated. The franchise network came later, partly from someone else's idea, at a time when Krigsner had no money to open shops himself and let other people take a share of the risk and of the reward.

You may be holding a piece of work close because it feels safer, or because sharing it means writing down rules that do not exist yet. Krigsner's team wrote theirs from nothing. Letting someone else carry part of the work is not the same as losing it, and it may give you an evening back.

sources.title: História do início da marca no Brasil (Our history)
sources.supports: O Boticário as the old name for pharmacist; Krigsner's compounding pharmacy opened on 22 March 1977 in central Curitiba; the idea came from a course in Porto Alegre where hand compounding, mainly for dermatology, was being rediscovered; carpeted room, sofa, magazines and coffee instead of counters of medicines; the owners themselves at the counter; word of mouth; move from compounding prescriptions to O Boticário-branded products; creams beaten in a mixer his sister received as a wedding present; first products a moisturising cream, a shampoo, a seaweed bath foam and the cologne Acqua Fresca; first exclusive shop at Curitiba airport in 1979, made known by passing flight crews.

sources.title: O homem que perfumou o Brasil – e se tornou modelo de empreendedorismo (interview, 29 June 2024)
sources.publisher: Brazil Journal (Geraldo Samor and Pedro Arbex)
sources.supports: Krigsner's own account: when franchising began it did not exist in Brazil, with no contracts, rules or procedures, and 'A gente teve que criar do zero'; growth leveraged through third parties' capital; franchisees often put their life savings in; the first factory built up shed by shed as money came in; he had no time to plan; from the pharmacy days he saw a possibility of growth without knowing its size; the group's roughly 4,000 shops.

sources.title: Miguel Krigsner (Bloomberg Línea 500)
sources.supports: Krigsner, Bolivian-Brazilian, graduated in pharmacy and biochemistry from the Federal University of Paraná in 1975 and two years later started the company with US$3,000.

sources.title: O Boticário: perfumando Brasília desde 1980 (2023)
sources.supports: O Boticário founded by the pharmacist Krigsner in 1977 behind a small door on a side street in Curitiba; first products a collagen cream, an elastin cream for stretch marks, a shampoo and a seaweed bath; first perfume in an amphora-shaped bottle; Brasília received the second shop in 1980, opened by Laura Oliveira after a trip to Curitiba, starting the franchise network (account of marketing director Bruna Buás); Acqua Fresca as the first fragrance.

sources.title: SV TÁ ON: a trajetória do Grupo Boticário e a estratégia no setor varejista (3 December 2025)
sources.supports: Franchising implemented in 1980; vice-president Rafael Marconi's account that Krigsner wanted to expand but had no capital, studied franchising when it did not yet exist in Brazil, and that the first shop at Curitiba airport spread the products through flight attendants who took them home as gifts.

cross_checks.claim: Krigsner opened O Boticário as a small compounding pharmacy on Rua Saldanha Marinho in Curitiba in 1977.
The first own-brand products were a few creams, a shampoo, a seaweed bath and a first fragrance, Acqua Fresca.
The brand opened a shop at Curitiba airport in 1979, and passing flight crews spread word of it.
Lacking capital, the company began franchising in 1980, building a franchise system that did not yet exist in Brazil.

research_notes: First franchise: sources disagree. Mercado & Consumo (2026) calls the 1979 airport shop the brand's first franchise; O Boticário's Portuguese site calls it the first exclusive shop; Jornal de Brasília (quoting the marketing director) says Brasília had the second shop, in 1980, opened by Laura Oliveira and starting the franchise network; SuperVarejo and Portuguese Wikipedia give 1980 for the start of franchising; the company's US blog says the first franchise store opened in 1982 (Portuguese Wikipedia gives 1982 as the year of the first factory, which may be the source of that confusion). The story calls the airport shop the brand's own shop and dates the franchise network to Brasília in 1980. First products: the Portuguese site lists a moisturising cream, a shampoo, a seaweed bath foam and Acqua Fresca; Jornal de Brasília lists a collagen cream, an elastin cream for stretch marks, a shampoo and a seaweed bath, with a first perfume in an amphora bottle; the story says 'a few creams'. The US$3,000 starting capital and the 1975 degree come only from Bloomberg Línea (English and Portuguese editions, one publisher), so they are attributed to it; Krigsner's partners at the start are not named in the sources, and the story says only that 'the owners' served customers. The mixer and the sister's wedding present are the company's own account, attributed as such. The Porto Alegre course and the shop's interior also come from the company's history. Krigsner's line 'A gente teve que criar do zero' is quoted in Portuguese from the Brazil Journal interview and glossed in English; his other remarks there (no time to plan, the factory built shed by shed, seeing a chance to grow from the pharmacy days) are paraphrased. The 4,000 shops figure is Brazil Journal's (2024); the group's own page speaks of the biggest beauty franchise in the world without a shop count. The episode closes before the group's later history, which is not told.
